dialogues.speaker: Yanbei
dialogues.text: With the improvements to their internal structure, the organizers should be able to attract more sponsors and expand to at least three times this size after just a few more events...

dialogues.speaker: Yanbei
dialogues.text: #Hey, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon! I've heard so much about you. What a pleasant surprise to see you guys here!

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: I'm just an ordinary clerk at the Liyue Ministry of Civil Affairs. I'm on a business trip to Sumeru and came by to check out the competition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon didn't think we'd run into friends from Liyue! Are you competing?

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Haha, I'll pass this time. I still have work to do. Being able to watch the event from the audience is satisfying enough already.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Although the event isn't as exciting as a real festival, I think it has potential. Maybe the organizers will make some internal adjustments in the future and attract more sponsors.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: When that time comes, the Beast Tamers Tournament should be able to grow and maybe even become mainstream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: More sponsors? Don't they already have that wealthy merchant, Elchingen, already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: His wealth may not be as mind-blowing as a successful merchant from Liyue, but it's substantial nonetheless.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: There will always be some doubt when you put all your eggs in one basket.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: I don't know Mr. Elchingen's background too well, but according to the information I've gathered, the origin of a large portion of his Mora remains unknown.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Hosting an event with funds of questionable origin may not sit well with some people.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: But I'm not from Fontaine, and it'd be impossible for me to know everything about every single Fontaine merchant. Maybe Elchingen earned his fortune gradually by doing business, and his peers didn't take notice of him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have a point. It wouldn't hurt to be a little more cautious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's a very thoughtful way of looking at it.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Thanks! Anyway, I'm just sharing my own thought process. If I were an employee working for the organizers, I would search for multiple sponsors to minimize the risk.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: I hope what I said didn't ruin your mood.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Yep. The way I see it, many of the organizers are capable individuals, but they, unfortunately, don't have a say in anything. Almost everything is decided by that researcher, Kautilya.

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: This event would undoubtedly be much better if he were to allow those individuals to make some decisions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's so complex... Paimon's having trouble following...

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Haha, that's alright, everyone has their own area of expertise. It's actually my job to analyze commercial events. Ordinary people should just try to enjoy the event for what it is.

choices.text: I'll let you get back to it. Goodbye...

response.speaker: Yanbei
response.text: Sure. You two seem like you have a lot to do as well. Let's grab a cup of tea when you have the time!
